title: From integrability to many-body quantum chaos through a Markovian bath
abstract: Recent examples have confirmed the common belief that quantum chaos is always suppressed in the presence of an environment. Here we show that this is not always the case. We compute the Lyapunov exponent of a $q$-body Majorana Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model coupled to a Markovian bath. Provided that the jump operators describing the bath are isotropic random $k > 2$-body Majoranas fields, the Lyapunov exponent is positive for any strength of the coupling to the bath. Interestingly, this also applies to $q=2$ where the SYK is integrable which indicates that many-body quantum chaos can be induced by the environment. Moreover, for $q > 2$, where the unitary dynamics is quantum chaotic, and sufficiently large $k$, the Lyapunov exponent increases with the coupling to the bath. Explicit analytical results are obtained in the $q=2$ and large $q$ limits. Our results put forward an alternate route to induce and control the generation of scrambling in quantum many-body systems which is of potential relevance in the design of quantum information devices.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates the interplay between quantum chaos and environmental coupling using the SYK model. By analyzing the Lyapunov exponent via OTOCs, the authors demonstrate that coupling to a specific type of bath can induce positive chaos even when the underlying system is integrable. This suggests a novel route to control scrambling in quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper challenges the common belief that coupling a quantum system to an environment always suppresses quantum chaos, investigating how this coupling affects the Lyapunov exponent.
main_result: The authors show that for specific bath couplings (isotropic random $k>2$-body Majoranas), the Lyapunov exponent remains positive and can even increase with the coupling strength, inducing quantum chaos.
method: The analysis employs the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, deriving Schwinger-Dyson equations and utilizing Out-of-Time-Order Correlators (OTOCs) to calculate the Lyapunov exponent.
model_or_system: The system studied is the $q$-body Majorana Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model coupled to a Markovian bath, whose dynamics are governed by a Lindblad master equation.
key_observables: Lyapunov exponent ($\lambda_L$), Out-of-Time-Order Correlators (OTOCs), and Green's functions ($G^>, G^<$).
important_parameters: Bath coupling strength ($\gamma$), number of Majorana bodies ($q$), and bath interaction order ($k$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the large $N$ limit and involves approximations up to $O(m\gamma^4)$ in the action expansion.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the calculated Lyapunov exponent ($\lambda_L$) versus dissipation strength ($\gamma$) for various $q$ and $k$ values, demonstrating the predicted enhancement of chaos.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from setting up the Lindblad dynamics and the path integral formulation to deriving the necessary Schwinger-Dyson equations, and finally calculating the OTOC kernels to determine the maximal eigenvalue ($\lambda_L$).
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete theoretical mechanism demonstrating that environmental coupling can actively induce or enhance quantum chaos, which is crucial for understanding quantum information processing in realistic, noisy settings.
